history.dynasty: Deva Dynasty of Sribhumi in Samatata (attributed patronage)
history.summary: NON-TEMPLE: KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED - like seq 2237 (the Teppakulam tank precedent), this row names archaeological rock CARVINGS, not a functioning temple: the group of Ganesha figures carved into perpendicular rock on the left bank of the stream at Unakoti (including a seated Ganesha about 22 ft high), the Durga-on-lion figure flanking the central Shiva head, and three enormous half-buried Nandi bull images. RELATED RECORDS: the Unakoti site is already documented as seq 1038 (id unakoti-rock-carvings); seq 2354 covers the site's central Shiva head (Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava). Recommend folding into seq 1038 or keeping as a sub-feature entry. The carvings are part of the 7th-9th-century bas-relief complex ascribed to the pre-Manikya period under Deva Dynasty patronage of Sribhumi in Samatata; Unakoti is ASI-protected and on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list (2022).

name: Ganesha-Durga-Nandi Rock Carvings, Unakoti
town: Unakoti (near Kailashahar; CSV town 'Unakoti' is the site name, ~8-9 km from Kailashahar town)
town_description: Unakoti is a forested hill site in Unakoti district, Tripura, about 8-9 km from the subdivision town of Kailashahar and roughly 125 km from Agartala. It is Tripura's prime tourist spot: an ASI-protected open-air Shaivite pilgrimage site of 7th-9th-century rock-cut carvings in a green, landscaped forest setting, on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list since 2022.

travel.airport: Nearest major airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala, about 125-140 km by road (verify); Kailashahar has a small non-scheduled airstrip (verify).
travel.railway: Kumarghat (about 27-30 km) or Dharmanagar (about 41 km) are the nearest railheads; hire a car onward (verify).
travel.road: About 8-9 km from Kailashahar; roughly 125 km from Agartala by road (verify). The site involves ~350 steps up and down - difficult for elderly visitors.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, the dry season; the Ashokastami Mela in March-April draws thousands.
visitor_information.opening_hours: No entry fee and no officially published hours reported; visit during daylight hours (verify). Carry water and food - no shops at the site.
